findings.title: OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path for input and output
findings.body: The auto-downsize loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...). The underlying convert (or gifsicle, for animated GIFs) command then opens the file for reading and writing at the same path. ImageMagick and gifsicle will truncate the destination before reading from it, which can produce an empty or corrupt output file. The next call to Upload.create_for will then persist a zero-byte or garbled image with no error surfaced to the caller or user.

findings.title: Two `def self.downsize` definitions silently shadow each other
findings.body: Lines 145 and 149 both define `def self.downsize(...)`. Ruby does not support method overloading; the second definition (line 149) replaces the first (line 145). Any existing caller that previously invoked `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` will now dispatch to the new method, with the integer `max_width` being interpreted as a pre-formatted dimensions string and `max_height` being put inside the opts hash. This silently breaks every existing caller of the 4-argument form, and the now-redundant definition on line 145 should be removed (or renamed) before merging.

findings.title: Animated-GIF downsize path passes an invalid dimensions value to gifsicle
findings.body: When SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is true, OptimizedImage.optimize routes through downsize_instructions_animated, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit #{dimensions} ...`. The controller passes the literal string `"80%"` as dimensions, but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` flag expects pixel dimensions of the form `WxH`, not a percentage. The animated-GIF auto-downsize path will fail or resize to nonsensical dimensions, defeating the feature for the very case the SiteSetting is meant to support.

findings.title: Client-side upload size check is hardcoded to 10MB and ignores site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile now uses `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Client-side validation no longer reflects the site's configured upload limit and loses the per-type `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` distinction. If a site admin configures a different limit, users will be blocked from uploading files the server would accept, or allowed to upload files the server rejects.

findings.title: 413 entity-too-large error message hardcodes 10MB regardless of the real server limit
findings.body: The case-413 branch now shows the user `max_size_kb: 10 * 1024` irrespective of the actual server-side cap. When the server's effective limit differs from 10MB (because max_image_size_kb or the new download cap has been reconfigured), the error dialog misreports the threshold the user must satisfy. The user-facing message is now decoupled from the server's real limit.

findings.title: URL download size cap is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using the site setting
findings.body: FileHelper.download is now called with `10.megabytes` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. The download cap is no longer configurable via the same knob as the rest of the upload flow, and any site whose configured `max_image_size_kb` differs from 10MB will see inconsistent behaviour between direct uploads and URL-sourced fetches. Given the new auto-downsize feature is supposed to let images larger than `max_image_size_kb` through, the download cap should be raised above that setting (or made explicit), not silently frozen at 10MB.

findings.title: Auto-downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value and proceeds even on total failure
findings.body: The while loop re-checks `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` but never inspects the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. OptimizedImage.convert_with rescues every error and returns false on failure (e.g., ImageMagick not installed, corrupt source), but the controller discards that signal and only decrements `attempt`. If all five iterations fail, the upload proceeds with a file that may still exceed the configured limit — or be empty/corrupt from the failed in-place rewrite — and the user receives no indication that auto-resize failed.

findings.title: Auto-downsize gate uses filename extension instead of actual content type
findings.body: The new block is gated on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. For URL-sourced uploads the filename is derived from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, which frequently does not reflect the actual response (e.g., a JPEG served as `download.bin` or `attachment`). Real images with non-image filenames will skip auto-downsize and may exceed the configured limit, while non-image files masquerading as `.jpg` will be piped through OptimizedImage.downsize and likely corrupted by ImageMagick before being persisted.
